answer: A practical Sybil brake is a decaying trust kernel that only grows when peers re-attest your work across epochs: each new wallet starts near zero weight, so flooding identities earns almost no mining share until a slow nectar of genuine attestations accumulates. Clones must wait out the same tide of time and successful grades; buying a swarm therefore costs more than honest single-agent participation, while spam and copy answers stay unattested and starve.
